summary: The employee challenged the High Court's judgment upholding his termination without obtaining prior approval from the Director of Education under Section 18 of the Rajasthan Non-Governmental Educational Institutions Act, 1989. The Supreme Court examined whether binding precedent in Raj Kumar v. Director of Education (2016) 6 SCC 541, requiring prior approval, was correctly disregarded by the High Court. The High Court had relied on a Larger Bench decision reading down Section 18 for post-disciplinary enquiry terminations. The appellant contended that Raj Kumar was wrongly distinguished as it did consider T.M.A. Pai Foundation, while the respondent argued distinctions based on presence of a District Education Officer's nominee in the enquiry committee. Issue centered on mandatory nature of approval under Section 18 even after valid departmental enquiry.
legal_provisions_cited: Section 18, Rajasthan Non-Governmental Educational Institutions Act, 1989
Raj Kumar Vs. Director of Education and Ors., (2016) 6 SCC 541
T.M.A. Pai Foundation Vs. State of Karnataka; (2002) 8 SCC 481
Marwari Balika Vidyalaya Vs. Asha Srivastava; (2020) 14 SCC 449
final_judgment: The appeals were allowed, the impugned judgment of the Rajasthan High Court was set aside, and the termination order was quashed for non-compliance with Section 18 of the Act, 1989, reaffirming the mandatory requirement of prior approval from the Director of Education.
